message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the most recent common ancestor of the two families **Felidae** (cats) and **Equidae** (horses, donkeys, zebras).  

Both families belong to the order **Carnivora** (Felidae) and **Perissodactyla** (Equidae), respectively. These two orders are part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which also includes orders such as Cetartiodactyla (even‑toed ungulates and cetaceans), Chiroptera (bats), and others.

So, the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatherian clade—a small, likely insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago during the late Cretaceous.
